entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, 2021, paragraphs 25-27
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V of 21 May 2013 On Personal Data and their Protection
entries.why_here: Input validation rejects impossible applicant values before inference so that screening relies only on reliable, accurate, and necessary data.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, 2021, paragraphs 28-30
entries.instrument: Constitution of the Republic of Kazakhstan (adopted 30 August 1995, as amended)
entries.why_here: Hiding name and university removes identity cues that produced a +2.5 score gap favoring flagship universities (p = 0.002) and 10.0% decision flips on gender-coded names.

entries.principle: Respect for human autonomy and informed consent
entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, 2021, paragraphs 32-34
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V of 21 May 2013 On Personal Data and their Protection
entries.why_here: Pre-model refusal blocks unauthorized screening purposes, minors under 18, unconsented profiles, and prompt-injection payloads without calling the LLM.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, 2021, paragraphs 37-43
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V of 21 May 2013 On Personal Data and their Protection
entries.why_here: The append-only JSONL log records controls, hashes, and outcomes for every request so decisions can be audited later without duplicating raw applicant PII.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, 2021, paragraphs 35-36 and 43
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V of 21 May 2013 On Personal Data and their Protection (and Administrative Procedural and Process-Related Code No. 350-VI of 29 June 2020)
entries.provision: Law No. 94-V Article 24(1)(4) and Article 24(1)(6); APPC Article 73(1)
entries.why_here: Routing borderline scores (45-60), unparseable outputs, and protected-attribute rationales to human reviewers preserves the applicant's right to contest automated outcomes.
